questions.answer: Course match, research opportunities.

questions.answer: Most information was easy but for information about leaving Denmark was not easy to know.

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: many courses are not available for exchange students.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: 1. Looked though the course catalog and found suitable courses. 2. Applied at the university's system. 3. Got approval

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The exchange office helped me to contact the course lecturer about joining the course.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered almost every course i wanted except one cognitive course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Before deciding the destination university, ask the university's available courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Level: 500 and 600
The courses were very intense. The workload was big and I found I was busy every day.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was more intense compared with UCPH. The teacher gave you more assignments and but gave you less freedom. In UCPH you can make your plan more flexible.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Social network analysis for computer scientists
2. Evolutionary Algorithms
3. Audio processing and indexing
4. Advanced typology
5. Language documentation

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Social network analysis for computer scientists. The workload of this course is very intense but you can learn a lot about network science. And it's very practical for many real world scenes.

questions.answer: The train cost between my dorm and the campus.

questions.answer: Transportation fee. They don't have discounts for students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many clubs at the orientation week including sports, workshop and music.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join more workshops and meet new people. Increase your connection.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to different cities like Utrecht or the Hague to explore museums and local restaurants.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yeah it was easy. Netherlands has a very international culture so i feel it was easy to get used to the local life.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really. I got used to the local culture easily.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are more extrovert and like to talk with each other.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Think deeply about why you want to go for an exchange. Don't just follow others' steps.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check which courses are only for their students but not for exchange students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Be more aware of what I should know and what I will do in the future and where I want to go.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: socialising with others. Sometimes I didn't know how to make new friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
